column1: # ID | status | note

BASE-1|Removed|Built in the first pass as a CPU speed setting (Auto, Full, Balanced, Eco) and taken out again at the owner's request before the fork was ever run: the cores stay at the kernel's 1.8 GHz, as under the stock app. Nothing in the fork touches cpufreq, and `Platform::cpu_limit()` is gone from the base.

BASE-2|Implemented in part|The screen thread now sleeps on a futex and is woken by controls, notes from outside and screenshot requests, instead of polling every 4 ms. After a change it draws 8 more frames at falling rates instead of 30 at 60 fps. With no control in use it draws at the app's `frame_interval()` (new setting SCREEN > Refresh, 30 fps by default). A still screen is still drawn 10 times a second: skipping that needs the dependency tracking described under UI-5. Review before the commit: a control used while a frame is being drawn now gets a frame of its own at the fast rate, where before (and in the original) it could wait out a still screen's 100 ms. And while a control has been used in the last 300 ms every frame comes at the fast rate, whether or not the frame changed: what a control does often shows a frame later, and the first version of this loop could then wait 100 ms.

BASE-3|Implemented|New setting SCREEN > Dim after (default 2 min): the backlight goes to its lowest level and the pad and button lights low. The level before the first change is restored on exit and by `restore-stock.sh`. A loop still heard in the Looper counts as something playing, so the lights stay up for it. A backlight left dimmed by a killed app is put back when the next one starts (`Platform::recover()`). Both were added in the review before the commit. The Power button ends the dimmed state as any other control does.

BASE-4|Implemented|MIDI clock, Active Sensing and MTC quarter frames no longer wake the screen. Notes and controllers from outside still do, and so do Start, Continue and Stop, so the screen shows a transport started from outside at once.

BASE-5|Implemented in part|`-mcpu=cortex-a55`, `-fno-trapping-math` and `-Wl,-z,now` are on. **`-fno-math-errno` is left out: measured, it changes the DSP bench's output**, so the auditor's "bit-exact expected" was wrong for that flag. With the two kept flags the bench output and the self-test audio are identical to the original build's. Section garbage collection was not tried. Second pass: `-O3` for the engine was measured too. It ran 4 % fewer instructions and changed the bench's output, so the engine stays at `-O2`.

BASE-6|Not implemented|Several of Melodee's timers count service passes (for example `++ticks % 600` for 3 s in `ProjectStore` and `SampleLibrary`), so a slower loop needs each of them changed to clock time first.
BASE-7|Not implemented|See LIGHT-3.
BASE-8|Implemented in part|Eager binding (`-Wl,-z,now`) is on. Memory locking and the audio thread's priority are unchanged: both need a dropout test on the device.
BASE-13|Implemented|The frame timer is disarmed in `stream_off()` and `close_device()`.

HOST-1|Not implemented|The largest remaining saving for a stopped or sparse project. It changes the main mix path and its tail rule needs listening tests on the device, so it was left for a pass that can be measured.
HOST-2|Not implemented|The threshold was set by the author from measurements on the device (`docs/ROADMAP.md`, P2); changing it needs the same.
HOST-3|Implemented in part|Case (a) is fixed: the workers are told to stay awake for a keyed run only when two or more tracks wait. Cases (b) and (c) are unchanged.
FX-2|Implemented|Bit-exact: 370 million gains compared against the original expressions, including every float within 20,000 steps of each threshold (`.local/checks/compressor_exact.cpp`).

SMP-1|Implemented|The pager sleeps on a futex while no stream is open and is woken by `open()`, `restart()`, `close()`, `flush()` and `stop()`. With a stream open it looks every millisecond as before.

MODEL-1|Not implemented|Its cost falls with the frame rate: at the default Refresh of 30 fps the copy runs half as often while playing. Gating it needs a change counter on every writer of the project.
MODEL-5|Implemented|The lane's own length is used directly; identical as long as each key has one lane, which `set_lane_length` guarantees.
LIGHT-1|Implemented|Uses `span()`.
LIGHT-3|Not implemented|`Shell::lights()` also runs about twenty housekeeping ticks; each has to be checked for an assumption about the 5 ms period before the tick slows.
LIGHT-4|Implemented|New setting PADS > Pad brightness (100, 75, 50, 25 %), and the lights go low with Dim after. `SurfaceLights` gained `scale()` and `rest()`.
LIGHT-5|Implemented|While SysEx goes out the thread is woken a millisecond on, not at a time already past.

LIGHT-6|Implemented in part|Thirteen command types that only mirror state or carry a gesture no longer mark the project changed: `MidiAudio`, `Monitor`, `LoopMonitor`, `InputTaken`, `RecordGain`, `RecordSource`, `KeyedRoot`, `ExtSync`, `MtcIn`, `RepeatKey`, `ArpKey`, `PunchOn`, `PunchOff`. `PunchDepth`, `MidiSync`, `MidiTrack` and `FlexBeat` are left as they were, because for each I found a path where the command is the only thing that marks a real edit. Review before the commit: with `PunchOn` and `PunchOff` exempt, nothing marked a change of the Pad FX bank or target as unsaved (in the original the next punch's command did, by accident). `set_punch_target()` and `step_punch_bank()` now mark the project themselves.
SHELL-1|Implemented|`MidiAudio` is exempt (see LIGHT-6), which ends the save-every-second loop.
IO-1|Implemented|`ProjectStore::scan` keeps each project's track count and tempo by path, modification time and size; a saved file is always read again.
IO-2|Implemented|The folder is re-listed every 3 s only while something reads the listing; a card change, a file Melodee wrote, a browse or the page opening still lists it at once.
IO-3|Not implemented|Needs a change counter in the Looper engine, which I did not read closely enough to place safely.
IO-7|Implemented|The idle wait is 100 ms instead of 25 ms. See IO-14 for the bug found in the same loop.
IO-14|Implemented|The predicate is now `(take_wanted && !taking)` and the wait is 25 ms during a take.
PLUG-1|Not implemented|The author's deliberate behaviour (plug-ins that follow the transport); TRANSPORT off already gives the sleeping behaviour per plug-in.

PLUG-2|Implemented|The host still spins for every command, but a process block whose reply outlasts the spin makes the next 64 blocks wait on the futex at once; then one spins again, so a plug-in that has become quicker is caught again. The bridge spins 1,000 loads after a reply instead of 4,000, enough for a command that follows at once (a block rendered in parts, a run of parameter reads), and then waits with no timeout, so an idle bridged plug-in no longer wakes 10 times a second. Bit-exact: `.local/checks/bridge-wait.sh` runs Melodee's `Vst2BridgeInstance` against `vst2_bridge32` built for aarch64 and a fixture plug-in with a set DSP time; the output hashes are the same before and after in every scenario (steady blocks, blocks in two parts, parameter reads between blocks), and an idle bridge went from 9 wake-ups a second to 0. The VM's CPU times are too noisy to put a number on the saving (two rounds of the same build differed by 2-3x); by the loop counts, a slow plug-in's host spin (20,000 loads) now runs on 1 block in 65, and the bridge's spin after every block is a quarter of what it was. Not yet measured on the MPC with a real armv7 plug-in.

SMP-9|Implemented|Second pass. `held_run()` in `sampler.cpp` plays the frames of a voice that holds its sustain, forwards and unfiltered, without the per-frame tests and the envelope's step, for `run_plain()` and `zone_run_plain()`. Measured: 17 % fewer instructions for the bench's busy project, the output the same to the bit. The tests compare it with the loop frame by frame (`held_runs` off) for kits and keygroups.

SMP-3|Implemented in part|Second pass. Step A: a Pad FX that is off moves its history on in one or two copies instead of a frame at a time. Measured with the two changes below it in the table of the second pass. Step B (one shared history) is not done.

FX-4|Implemented in part|Second pass. The echoes' SYNC look-up (`sync_back()`, two calls into another file for every frame) is made once a call in Echo, Tape echo and Ping pong; each frame keeps its glide. The other sites are unchanged: each has to be shown to compile to the same sums, and the one tried next did not (FX-3).

FX-3|Tried and withdrawn|Second pass. Working the swings' sines out ahead of the frames, with the same arguments, changed what Chorus, Flanger and Tape echo played against the original build (the two ways agreed with each other inside one build: the compiler fused the surrounding sums differently once the code had moved) and saved no instructions. Reverted.

HOST-4|Implemented in part|Second pass. Step 3 for four loops: a gain that does not move in the block is read once (the track's pan stage, its way to the master and Knob FX, its sends, the buses' returns). Same sums, same output. No flag change: `-O3` on the engine was measured, saved 4 % and changed what the bench played, so it is not used.
